questions.q: What does Grant say about your giving style?
a: It is fluid and shifts with the person and situation
It is fixed by your personality early in life
It depends mostly on how much money you earn
It is usually the opposite of how you were raised
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we all have a main style but adapt our behavior to situations and people.

questions.q: What did the Manchester United jersey example show?
a: Fans were three times more likely to help a fellow supporter
Fans helped strangers more than they expected
Team loyalty made people less generous overall
People only help when others are watching
questions.why: Lesson 1 says similarity and shared identity strongly affect how generous we are.

questions.q: What is powerless communication, according to Grant?
a: Asking questions and seeking advice instead of asserting yourself
Hiding your expertise so others underestimate you
Agreeing with people until they start to trust you
Letting others make every decision for the group
questions.why: Lesson 2 says giving up power creates zero resistance and makes people want to help.

questions.q: How did the woman facing relocation use powerless communication?
a: She asked HR what they would do and gained access to a jet
She demanded a transfer and threatened to quit
She negotiated a higher salary before moving
She asked colleagues to cover her coursework
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes her asking the HR manager what he would do, which led to private jet access.

questions.q: What protects givers from burning out, according to Grant?
a: Seeing the impact their help has on other people
Working fewer hours than takers do
Keeping their generosity private
Learning to say no more often
questions.why: Lesson 3 says givers do not need fewer hours, they need to see the impact they create.
